title: Curated-source identification: mark/identify canonical articles for the hybrid resolver
priority_note: The resolver (31.2) needs a defined notion of 'curated/canonical' — the knowledge subsystem has category/scope enums and hubs but no explicit curated-answer marker. This story supplies it. No dependencies.

background.reference: GitHub issues #305 + #306 (same feature); Second Brain hub 820602df (Cloud Codes OKF+RAG), okf-open-knowledge-format memory. Composes the EXISTING knowledge subsystem (lib/loopctl/knowledge.ex, okf.ex) — do NOT re-architect embeddings.
background.includes: loopctl articles have category (Ecto.Enum), status, scope, and hub/link structure, plus OKF export/import — but no flag distinguishing an AUTHORED/CANONICAL answer from a probabilistic chunk. The hybrid resolver must prefer curated over fuzzy, so 'curated' needs a concrete, queryable definition.

story.i_want_to: define and expose which published articles count as 'curated/canonical' (a configured curated category set and/or explicit curated marker, plus OKF-index/hub membership) with a helper to identify them
story.so_that: the hybrid resolver can prefer a curated answer over a fuzzy chunk with a clear, testable rule

rationale: The whole point of #305/#306 is 'prefer curated over fuzzy when both exist' — which is undefinable without a concrete curated-source rule. Basing it on the existing category enum + hub/OKF membership (rather than a brand-new subsystem) keeps this a thin resolution layer, per the issue's 'compose existing pieces' constraint, while making 'curated' auditable and tenant-scoped.

acceptance_criteria.description: A curated-source rule is defined: a published article is 'curated' if its category is in a configured curated set (e.g. reference/playbook/pattern hubs) AND/OR it carries an explicit curated marker. If a new marker is used, add it via migration (nullable boolean/field on articles) with tenant scoping; if category-based, no migration. The choice is documented with rationale.

Loopctl.Knowledge.curated?/1 (and a scoped list/query helper) returns whether an article is curated and lists a tenant's curated sources, reusing existing published-status + category + hub/OKF-index membership signals.
Curated identification is tenant-scoped: a curated article of tenant A is never surfaced as curated in tenant B's scope.
Only PUBLISHED articles can be curated (a draft/archived canonical source is not treated as a curated answer).

test_cases.name: curated? reflects the configured rule
expected_results: the published reference/hub is curated; the low-category one is not; the draft is not (published-only)

technical_notes: Reuse Loopctl.Knowledge category (@category_values) + status + hub/link + OKF membership; prefer category-set config over a new column if it covers the cases (avoids a migration).
If a marker column is added, migration must tenant-scope + enable RLS consistency with articles.
This is the resolution-layer definition only — no embedding/vector changes (out of scope per #305).
